Tactus LLM Guidance (Canonical)

This file is intended for AI assistants and automated tooling. It describes the
canonical concepts and patterns for writing correct, modern Tactus code.

If you are producing docs or examples, also consult:
- docs/model-primitive.md
- README.md
- SPECIFICATION.md

================================================================================
MODEL PRIMITIVE
================================================================================

One-sentence definition:
A Model is Tactus's stateless prediction interface: typed input -> typed output,
with a registry-backed lifecycle for training, versioning, and evaluation.

Model vs Agent:
- Use a Model for classification/extraction/scoring ("input in, output out").
- Use an Agent for multi-turn reasoning and tool use.

Canonical runtime call pattern (always use this):

  local m = Model("imdb_nb")
  local result = m({text = input.text})
  local out = result.output or result

Do NOT:
- Do not invent a "Model.predict()" DSL method. Models are called like functions.

Training config (Option A, canonical):
Training lives inside the same Model block under "training".

  Model "imdb_nb" {
    type = "registry",
    name = "imdb_nb",
    version = "latest",
    input = { text = "string" },
    output = { label = "string", confidence = "float" },
    training = { data = {...}, candidates = {...} }
  }

CLI (canonical):
- Train:
    tactus train file.tac --model imdb_nb
- Evaluate (registry-backed):
    tactus models evaluate file.tac --model imdb_nb

Registry tags (canonical):
- latest
- candidate/<candidate_name>

Testing story (canonical):
Specs should test procedure logic, not model quality.
Use Mocks for deterministic CI (conditional mocking is preferred).

Dependencies:
Do not assume heavy ML deps in the core install.
- Core runtime: pip install tactus
- sklearn training: pip install "tactus[ml]"
- HF training: pip install "tactus[hf]"

================================================================================
AGENT PRIMITIVE
================================================================================

Agents are stateful multi-turn runtimes. They can use tools and iterate.
Keep deterministic control flow in Procedures and use Agents for the
non-deterministic steps that benefit from intelligence.
